Listen to this article Share The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed unwholesome, banned, fake and adulterated products worth N8 billion confiscated in the course of its operations in the North Central Zone. The destruction exercise was carried out on Thursday during the North Central Zonal Destruction of NAFDAC regulated products in Lafia, Nasarawa State. Mojisola Adeyeye, the Director-General of NAFDAC represented by the Joseph Edor, the Deputy Director in charge of North Central Zone said the bulk of the destroyed products were predominantly banned alcoholic beverages in low volumes of less than 200ml (20cl). Adeyeye explained that studies by researchers had shown that due to the availability, affordability and portability of such pack sizes, they had become major products of abuse and addiction among Nigerians, especially youths and underage school children. She noted that research had also shown that early exposure to alcohol affects the brain and other vital organs such as the liver and kidneys, stymies the brain resulting in mental retardation and brain damage, which in turn leads to poor performance of pupils and students in school, low productivity and several illnesses. She said, “It was based on these abuses, addiction and adverse effects that the Agency banned the production, distribution and sale of alcoholic beverages in sachets, PET and glass bottles below 200ml, hence the raid and confiscation from manufacturing outfits, sales outlets, markets and motor parks.” Other products destroyed include expired, fake and unwholesome food, drugs and cosmetics confiscated during daily operations. The NAFDAC DG said the Agency has the mandate of protecting and promoting public health by ensuring that only the right quality, safe and efficacious drugs, food, cosmetics, medical devices, water and other regulated products are manufactured, imported, distributed, advertised or used in Nigeria. She said in order to achieve the mandate, the Agency through its officers carries out inspections, investigations, enforcement, product registration and laboratory analysis. The DG appreciated other law enforcement organisations, sister agencies, associations and stakeholders for their continuous collaboration, especially in intelligence sharing and security cover during operations. Gbaoron is the Plateau State correspondent for BusinessDay and a seasoned journalist with a decade of experience covering sub-national affairs across Taraba, Adamawa, Nasarawa, Benue, Plateau, and other states. He holds both National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) in Mass Communication from Fidel Polytechnic, Gboko. Over the years, he has participated in numerous media trainings and workshops spanning various areas of reporting, strengthening his expertise in economic and political reporting, community-level governance, development stories, and conflict-sensitive journalism. He is a member of Correspondent Chapel in Plateau state, a member of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), he is also a Rotarian and a member of Plateau Club 1921.
